posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Has anyone used a good Fresnel lens for a collimator for a simple single beam hologram? I have one from an overhead projector. It is very rigid and was used as an imaging lens in the projector. Pros and cons welcome.

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
Run a spatially filtered beam through it and see what comes out. It won't look too pretty.

Because of the stepped rings there is no smooth transformation of the wavefront and the beam won't be completely collimated across the profile. See for instance "Seeing the Light" by Falk, Brill, and Stork, p.93, Figure 3.29.

Fresnel lenses are typically used as field lenses like in the overhead or lighthouses (their original application) to manage light sources and are rarely if ever used to form images.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Thank Ed, I will. I kind of thought there might be some uneveness in the shape of rings but I have not looked myself and wonded how much of an effect it might have on a single beam. From the sounds of it, it must be severe. Thinking about it now, I guess all the imperfections of the groves show up also. Well, I guess that leaves mounting my 16 inch colimator overhead. Dang thing has some weight to it. The negative is that collimator has a focal length of 75 inches.

posts.author: DJ Mathson
posts.content_md: John, wouldn´t it be better to have the collimator (I assume it is a mirror) on the table and have a large front surface mirror relaying the collimated beam?

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Well yes, but my the only collimators I have are 16" - 75" fl which is heavy and a 5" (not sure of fl exactly). My set up is overhead. My table 80" by 40". This presents problems. I was hoping to put the Fresnel which has a short fl and is light in the existing set up.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFP:** Well yes, but my the only collimators I have are 16" - 75" fl which is heavy and a 5" (not sure of fl exactly). My set up is overhead. My table 80" by 40". This presents problems. I was hoping to put the Fresnel which has a short fl and is light in the existing set up.

Fold the beam after your spatial filter. That's what I do. As long as the mirror after the SF is clean you'll never see any problems. You'll also want a 1/2 wave plate to put the polarization back the way it needs to be.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Well, I did look at the Fresnel lens with and expanded laser beam and it surely shows all the "rings". A Fresnel lens would not even be good to use for object illumination. Although it looks interesting and making a colorful hologram (maybe the broken mirror) with a Fresnel reference may add an interesting effect. Not sure why I never just simply put the Fesnel in the beam and looked at it before.
